name: Council
blurb: A council of Claude agents that reads 155 names every week and holds what it judges the best portfolio.

final.statement: First portfolio, built to survive election week and NVDA's Nov 17 print. The core is cash-backed quality that is mispriced or low-beta: MSFT, GOOGL, ADBE, INTU, TMUS and JPM, with a health care sleeve held to 18%, not stacked to 25%. The AI-capex cluster (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA) totals 21%, under the risk manager's 25% line. GOOGL stays at 5% because the red team is right: a 50% net margin over a 33% operating margin flatters the P/E, and there is no base yet. I'm cutting MU, MELI, LLY, CRM and the sub-2% noise. XLE and IEF are hedges, not convictions. Cash is 21%. I'll add risk when VIX/VIX3M drops below 0.9 and semis hold their lows.
final.summary: A barbell of cheap, accelerating, cash-generative tech (MSFT, GOOGL, ADBE, INTU, NVDA) and low-drawdown defensives (JNJ, ABBV, XLV, BRK-B, TMUS, JPM), with oil and duration hedges. Health care is capped at 18% and the AI-capex cluster at 21%. Cash is 21% to absorb midterm, semi read-through and Nov 17 event risk.

final.changes: First portfolio, built from scratch with $100k. It follows the consensus core but cuts names under 2% (MU, MELI, LLY, CRM, V, MRK, KO, NEE, RSP, ETN) to reduce noise and event risk. GOOGL stays at 5% below its cap, BRK-B is trimmed, health care is held to 18%, and the AI-capex cluster to 21%. Cash is 21%, above the 15% minimum.

dissent.view: GOOGL is a falling knife at 17.5% below its 50-day; wait for a reclaim. Overruled at small size because valuation and revenue acceleration justify a starter.
Wanted MELI, META, MU and FCX as hated quality and called the health care core crowded. Overruled because of the Brazil rate shock, META's S&P outlook and peak-cycle memory risk.
Wanted LLY 5%, MU 4% and MELI 3%. Overruled: LLY at RSI 80 is covered by XLV, and MU and MELI fail risk caps and event timing.
Wanted ~55% defensives including KO, PG, MRK and NEE, and IEF at 8%. Overruled: staples are crowded at 25-28x, and duration at RSI 80 is limited to 5%.
Wanted RSP 8%, NEE and XLP. Overruled to avoid overlap with core holdings and crowded defensives.
Wanted CRM and UBER. Overruled: both are decelerating into binary prints (UBER Nov 4, CRM late November).

atlas.name: Atlas
atlas.mandate: You own the top-down view: growth, inflation, the Fed and liquidity, rates, the dollar, credit and the business cycle. Decide how much risk the portfolio should carry and which sectors the regime favours. You may hold cash, bonds, gold or defensives when the regime says so.

nova.name: Nova
nova.mandate: You hunt for compounding growth: revenue acceleration, expanding margins, durable secular demand and pricing power. You accept a premium valuation when growth earns it, but you must name the evidence that growth is accelerating, not just high.

anchor.name: Anchor
anchor.mandate: You protect against overpaying. You favour cash generation, balance-sheet strength, returns on capital and a margin of safety. Point out where the price already assumes perfection, and find quality that is mispriced.

pulse.name: Pulse
pulse.mandate: You read price and positioning: trend, relative strength across horizons, volatility, drawdowns and breadth. Momentum is one of the most robust effects in markets, so respect it, but flag exhaustion and crowding. Ground every claim in the numbers you were given.

raven.name: Raven
raven.mandate: You look where the crowd is not. Find hated or neglected assets whose news is improving faster than their price, and crowded favourites whose story is already fully priced. Disagreeing for its own sake is useless; bring a specific catalyst or a specific mispricing.

forge.name: Forge
forge.mandate: You are the specialist on semiconductors, AI infrastructure, cloud and software. Judge supply chains, capex cycles, pricing (memory, GPUs), competitive position and who actually captures the AI spend.

harbor.name: Harbor
harbor.mandate: You cover what holds up when growth stumbles: health care, staples, utilities, energy, gold, Treasuries and other real assets. Argue for the hedges and diversifiers the portfolio needs, and say what they cost in expected return.

scout.name: Scout
scout.mandate: You track what happens next: earnings dates, guidance changes, product launches, regulation, M&A, index changes and policy events. Favour names with a near-term catalyst that the market underestimates, and warn about event risk.
